So "Damp" is key and not wet. The longer your media can dwell through the damp state the more rapid the continuous growth rate.

Unlike soil medias you don't need a "dry out" phase if you have the dampness and air retention and all that just right. Their water requirements are almost nothing and the greatest loss is through evaporation so all they need is regular misting to prevent them from drying out completely. There are really good reasons to expect that they should get better results cloning. They basically take all of the work of nannying them for the most ideal conditions out of it for you and return it to the substrate, which is a resilient, sponge-like, polymerized bark material and full of beneficial bacteria with mild nutrients impregnated. The bark itself carries rooting hormones. All you have to do is keep the sponge damp. If you see mold on it, it's probably beneficial. I think it's a more advanced, fool proof approach with far superior results. I've got 100% germination rate on the last ones out of 14 or so.. I think one got too hot or I let it dry out too much, maybe both.
